summary: Phase 2: installed-first independent modules. Retain compatible installed versions/settings, stop unknown/incompatible inventory before downloads, and never call the broad Microsoft bundle normal setup.
action_notice: Human direct tasks or human-selected local Workstation setup only, with scoped approvals/native confirmations. Ordinary agents use source/mocks. No repair, automatic elevation/restart, policy/source bypass, upgrade or hidden Restore.

purpose.p: Choose only missing tools and independently approved SDK/extension/WSL modules without rewriting the machine's installed state.

All module targets are inventoried before any download/source/provider/installer activity. Missing targets are rechecked after approval; known installed targets are retained rather than redownloaded/upgraded.

starting_state.p: Phase 0 decisions and successful Preflight, safe reviewed checkout, previous vendor installers known stopped/completed, and an approved restart window if needed.
No-module bootstrap is nonmutating Core preview. Setup preview/User-run setup select one module; there is no blanket normal Microsoft preset.

steps.title: Select the local agent once, then approve real stages
steps.where: VS Code Chat › Local Windows session › Workstation setup

body.p: The native repository agent reads existing scripts/catalog/tasks, checks prior installer/reboot safety, inventories before network Preflight, and invokes only needed sequential modules. It explicitly separates dependency Restore, no-restore checks and approved local startup/requests; you do not pick every task or paste every command.

The human approves scoped installations/downloads/launches and answers native prompts. WSL changes, Ubuntu, licensed Docker, modernization and images are separate decisions. Missing interactive tools/prompts stop at the exact blocker; the agent never types approval answers or suppresses permissions.

Resume only after known installer/vendor/reboot outcomes. Refresh inventory and approvals, never blindly retry or infer success from cancellation/logs/exit 0. Default local Python/current Java/Go acceptance does not hide missing WSL or unapproved full-profile/source state.

steps.expect: One human-selected local agent and auditable existing terminal work with real approval pauses. Live VS Code selection/tool/native-confirmation acceptance is not yet proven by static tests.

steps.title: Manual fallback: preview one needed named module

body.p: For manual operation, select Core, Python, Java, Go, Extensions, WSL, Ubuntu, Docker or Modernization. Review all target version/location/inventory states before any apply decision.

callout.text: Compatible installed: retain/skip before download. Registered incompatible or unknown: retain and stop without downloads. Aliases/caches or arbitrary unknown portable paths are not installation proof.

steps.expect: A local installed/missing/unknown plan, not an executed install or blanket agent permission.

steps.title: Core: confirm only genuinely missing targets
steps.where: Terminal › Run Task › Install core tools

body.p: Core covers VS Code, Git, GitHub CLI, Copilot CLI, uv, PowerShell 7, Node LTS, Azure CLI, azd and kubectl. Existing compatible versions/settings/accounts are retained; no automatic upgrades or global PATH/profile/Copilot changes.

steps.expect: Per-target retained/installed/stopped outcomes. No fonts, PowerToys, NVM, Explorer/taskbar or other broad global tweaks.

steps.title: SDKs: Python, current Java and Go are independent
steps.where: Terminal › Run Task › Install Python SDK / Install Java SDK / Install Go SDK

steps.expect: Each selected SDK has its own reviewed inventory and confirmation; other modules remain untouched.

steps.title: Select Native essentials or the separate full extension scope
steps.where: Workstation setup approval or existing Extensions terminal route

body.p: Default Native uses only ms-python.python, ms-python.debugpy, redhat.java, vscjava.vscode-java-debug and golang.go. The same authoritative selection is used in inventory, recheck and Verify. Python Debugger bundles debugpy; Java language support is a debugger dependency.

Human/IT attests existing CLI/default-profile source/account routing and approved bundled dependencies before ExtensionSourceApproved. That flag is not a source override, acceptance proof or marketplace bypass.
The separate full default module still requires twelve extensions; choose that wider scope explicitly, never to make Native ready.

steps.expect: Only approved missing targets in the selected scope, retaining compatible installed IDs/versions/accounts/profile/settings.

steps.title: If the private marketplace path is unsupported, stop

callout.text: A private-marketplace banner proves neither denial nor compatibility. If existing CLI/profile routing is unsupported, stop acceptance. IT must supply compatible managed automated delivery; no public VSIX/source/account/profile bypass or twelve manual installs.

steps.expect: An explicit blocker and supported IT path, never a green acceptance inferred from a CLI list.

steps.title: WSL: inspect features and restart state before payloads
steps.where: Terminal › Run Task › Install WSL components

body.p: Use an approved Administrator context for feature actions when required; no automatic elevation. DISM is no-restart. Required/pending restart pauses before further downloads. Existing WSL runtime, distros, defaults and data are retained.
No silent WSL update, distro reset/launch or automatic reboot. wslc presence is not proof of runtime health or policy acceptance.

steps.expect: Explicit feature/runtime result or stopped-for-restart outcome; never a partially completed module reported as complete.

steps.title: Optional modules remain separate decisions
steps.where: Terminal › Run Task › Optional named module

body.p: Ubuntu is a separate optional module only after WSL/features/restart readiness. Docker Desktop requires explicit licensing approval. Modernization is Java 11 plus the optional thirteenth extension; it is not a manual upgrade of the legacy application.

callout.text: Legacy Microsoft bundle (optional) is broad upstream opt-in, not normal setup or partial-run recovery. Finish setup/Legacy SkipBase require confirmed successful legacy base plus reboot/resume. A force-closed original base is stopped partial, not successful completion or rollback.

steps.expect: Only the selected approved optional scope; installed shared tools/settings/accounts/distros remain retained.

steps.title: Observe target events, timeouts and uncertain vendor state

body.p: Read streamed target status, elapsed time, actual exit codes and the final module result. Per-target wait defaults to 7200 seconds; picker 3600/7200/14400, direct accepted range 300-14400. Those are wait limits, not completion promises.

Non-secret state/elapsed events live in `.showcase-setup\module-*.jsonl`, not raw request/vendor-output logging. Timeout/cancellation can leave elevated vendor-child state uncertain; do not blindly retry or kill all similarly named processes.

For the separately chosen legacy bundle, its base wait picker is 7200/14400/28800 seconds, default 14400. PID/lock/log activity is not success: final summary, flagged steps, key dismissal and actual reboot/resume matter.

steps.expect: A known complete/stopped/failed/uncertain result. Pause before the next module if vendor or restart state is unresolved.

expected.p: A truthful per-module installed-first outcome with existing compatible state retained. Setup modules themselves never Restore or launch; the named agent's later Restore/launch stages need separate approval. It never signs in or deploys.

success.p: Only after known module/vendor/restart outcomes, proceed to [save/reopen and Verify](page:setup-verify). Actual required readiness and intended extension profile acceptance are still necessary.

failures.symptom: Installed tool is invisible in the current terminal
failures.cause: Stale VS Code environment or known registration/path not represented on PATH
failures.fix: Use reported installed version/location. Save work and fully exit/reopen VS Code from Windows as appropriate; no reinstall or global PATH edit.

failures.cause: Registered state cannot safely satisfy the manifest
failures.fix: Retain it and stop before downloads. Report the mismatch for approved review; no automatic upgrade/replacement.

failures.cause: Vendor/elevated child completion or Windows feature state is uncertain
failures.fix: Stop further module downloads/retries. Establish the actual owned vendor/restart outcome with IT; no mass termination or automatic reboot.

failures.symptom: Stopped legacy base followed by a Finish request
failures.cause: Partial setup mistaken for successful base/reboot/resume
failures.fix: Do not run Finish/SkipBase. Preserve all installed state, inspect outcomes, and use reviewed installed-first module inventory for genuine missing targets.

recovery.p: Use [stopped-partial recovery](page:operate-recovery), never rollback or broad uninstall. Ordinary agents use source/AST/mocks only; the named local workflow resumes with fresh safety/inventory and new scoped approvals, never repair.

limitations.p: Hosted mock tests do not prove this laptop's vendor install, source/profile routing, runtime health, licence, restart or package readiness.

say: Installed software is discovered before any missing-target download.
Core, SDKs, extensions and WSL are independently confirmed modules.
Stopped partial is not completed setup, rollback or permission to Finish.
evidence_gaps: No live agent selection/tool use/native confirmation, module preview/apply, vendor/reboot outcome or enterprise source/profile acceptance is claimed for this laptop.
